messages:
Nia: Quick note — small smoke on rbk-3b-v2 shows backend-dependent rank flips, posting concise triage plan.
Sam: numbers?
Nia: Hosted int8 NDCG@10 -0.8% vs fp16; dedicated int8 -0.12%. Top1 swap hosted ~2.3%.
Ravi: Did you lock tokenization and candidate order?
Nia: Yes. command: 
```bash
eval_small --model rbk-3b-v2 --backends hosted,dedicated --qtypes int8,fp16 --cohort strat10k --seed 777 --keep-order --normalize
```
Sam: Suspect kernel numeric differences + microbatch order. Any evidence of token id drift?
Nia: Token ids serialized identical for a sample. Uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/rbk3b/v2/3105009999/
infra-bot: upload complete.
Ravi: Proposed quick experiments: 1) force hosted kernel to match dedicated; 2) run with prefix cache off; 3) rerun borderline set (margin<0.04) at 50k.
Nia: Filed INFRA-905 (kernel pin) and EVAL-412 (cache-off).
Sam: If kernel pin solves it, we should add a numeric-stability check in CI comparing int8 kernels across backends.
Nia: Agreed. I'll attach sample ids where flips occur (ids: 210, 4312, 8890) and follow up with results. :white_check_mark:
